task.description: Handle ISS-0403 directly per ORCH's sizing-rule direct-action exception (docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md Section10): exactly one file touched (test/letflow/secrets_test.exs), no new public function/module/@spec, no migration, no supervision-tree file touched, no tenant-data path (test-only), no production-code behavior change.

result.summary: Root cause already confirmed accurate by the issue's own filing (a property-test design flaw: refute String.contains?(ciphertext, plaintext) is a meaningless assertion once byte_size(plaintext) is small enough that coincidental containment becomes statistically likely, not a real leak signal). Fix: raised the containment check's minimum plaintext length threshold from > 0 to >= 8 bytes (documented inline with the probability math: N * (1/256)^k, negligible at k>=8 for any N used here). Added a dedicated regression test reproducing the exact originally-observed byte value (186) at byte_size 1, run 20 times in a loop to demonstrate the containment check is genuinely skipped rather than coincidentally passing. mix test test/letflow/secrets_test.exs run 6 times total (1 default + 5 different --seed values) plus once more with the new regression test: all green, 10-11 passed each time depending on whether the regression test's own run is counted. mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix format --check-formatted both clean.
